newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesian rupiah falls in late trading.
newsitem.headline: Indonesian rupiah falls in late trading.

text.p: Indonesia's rupiah was lower against the dollar in late trading on Friday amid ample liquidity and cautious sentiment after Thursday's protest by backers of ousted minority party leader Megawati Sukarnoputri, dealers said.
"Liquidity remained ample in the afternoon as the protest prompted some overseas rupiah selling, but the falls were somewhat limited due to weekly tax-payments," one bank dealer said.
Dealers said local operators were initially indifferent to the demonstration, but they followed suit after active rupiah selling by overseas operators.
Spot rupiah was last quoted at 2,360.70/60.90 against an opening of 2,358.50/59.50.
Another dealer said the spot rupiah rate was likely to range between 2,360.00 and 2,361.00 on Monday, with rupiah liquidity seen remaining ample as reflected in lower tom/next swap rate.
Tom/next was last traded at par/0.20 after an opening of 0.50/0.55 point, he said.
Overnight swap was also briefly traded at par before rising again to 0.10/0.30 points against an opening of 1.20/1.35.
Tomorrow and today rupiah were last quoted at 2,360.70/60.90 and 2,358.75/59.20 respectively.
Another dealer said overseas rupiah selling had more to do with the usual higher domestic demand for dollars due to year-end rather than the political protest which passed without incident.
Dealers, however, said overseas operators appeared to remain cautious over any potential tension following the protest.
It was the first organised opposition political protest in Jakarta since July when the city was rocked by the worst riots in 20 years.
Bank Indonesia raised its intervention band by one point to 2,356/2,548 and the conversion band by one point to 2,356/2,404 late on Friday.
